prompts.workshop: Use case stylized-concept. Create a new seamless-capable game terrain texture sheet for the user's fantasy dungeon repair workshop, four separate texture sprites. The first reference is for the design treatment only: dark recesses outside a readable top-down corridor, a narrow raised stone wall cap and a darker visible front wall face. Do not copy any characters, devices, art, level layout or actual pixels from it. The second reference is the user's workshop game art. Match its muted warm slate, soot charcoal and bronze palette, and its crisp digitally painted material detail. Square transparent canvas, exact 2×2 evenly spaced uniform square cells. Center of each sprite sits at 25% or 75% in each axis. Exactly one axis-aligned square texture per slot, wide empty transparent gutters and opaque rectangular swatches, no props, text, glow, border between swatches, or shadows outside tiles. Upper left: lighter worn grey stone capstone seen vertically above, broad shallow bevels and large stone planes, narrow subtle fine seams, usable as narrow corridor wall edges. Upper right: front-facing vertical dark slate masonry wall face, a carved warm highlight along top, large dark layered stone courses below, no ground, no perspective. Lower left: very dark uneven jagged compact charcoal rubble stone fill, low contrast inside black charcoal recess, edge dark and repeatable. Lower right: calm worn workshop flagstone floor seen straight above, medium warm grey with sparse worn fissures and barely visible tile joins. Orthogonal, no diagonal tile edges, no isometric diamond. The four original sprites will be clipped and used in a 2D grid game, generate art not a mockup.
prompts.workshop_finish_terrain: Use case stylized-concept. Production sprite sheet of nine fresh terrain tiles, for a premium fantasy dungeon repair-workshop 2D puzzle game. The reference shows the actual current room, its game camera and layout; redesign the artwork to give richer hand-painted materials and a clearer hierarchy. Draw only sprites, no board or UI. EXACT 3 columns x 3 rows on a square true-transparent canvas, all nine axis-aligned square texture swatches of equal width and height with generous transparent gutters. Centers at 1/6, 1/2 and 5/6 on each axis. Keep the swatches opaque from edge to edge, separate, and clear enough to use at about 100 pixels. Painterly stylized game art with chunky shapes, well-defined masonry and tasteful subtle surface wear, no noise or dramatic baked lighting. Warm antique brass, charcoal blue slate, warm taupe flagstones; warm-gold upper highlights and cool deep crevices. Layout is row-major. R1: (1) warm grey square smooth ashlar floor blocks with sparse grout lines, (2) same floor in a medium warm slate tone with staggered larger stones, (3) same floor with one little aged scorch trace and a clean partial fracture. All three floor swatches feel like different positions in the SAME WALKABLE ROOM FLOOR, similar brightness so placement looks intentional. R2: (1) horizontal ashlar wall cap made of three long large beveled gunmetal stones with restrained copper inset stripe on the long edge, (2) straight-on front-facing dark slate masonry wall face with clear three-dimensional depth, broad joints and a moulded copper-edged ledge across the top, (3) MASONRY COLUMN capital seen from directly above, square slightly larger corner block with broad beveled edges and a small restrained riveted iron corner clasp. R3: (1) irregular large dark basalt chunks fading to black in seams, (2) another dark rock variant with sparse smaller chipped stones, same low dark values, (3) square dark-mahogany and iron ANVIL PLINTH seen from above, robust riser rim and four iron rivets, no anvil included, used as a visual foundation for a nonwalkable decorative object. No numbers, text, icon, character, device, floor grid overlay, or full level. Avoid ornate glowing runes in walkable tiles.
